body:
`BachelierCalculator::theta()` used `gamma(spot)` in the diffusion term. The normal volatility in the calculator is the volatility of the forward, so the term needs the forward gamma; with the spot gamma it is off by a factor (F/S)² whenever the forward and the spot differ, that is, whenever r ≠ q. With the change, theta is the derivative of the price with respect to time to maturity, as `BlackCalculator::theta()` already is (it matches the same finite difference).

`vanna()` left out the discount factor that `vega()` includes, so it wasn't the derivative of `vega()`. It is now written in terms of `vega()`, as `BlackCalculator::vanna()` is. The header describes it as the sensitivity of vega to spot, but it takes no spot and the existing finite-difference test checks it against the forward, so I kept the forward.

Call with S = 98, K = 105, r = 4%, q = 1%, σ = 20, T = 1.5 (forward 102.51, discount 0.9418):

| | before | after | finite difference |
|---|---|---|---|
| theta | -4.34703 | -4.05962 | -4.05962 (price with T ± h) |
| vanna | 0.0020167 | 0.0018992 | 0.0018992 (vega with F ± h) |

For the put, theta goes from -1.35703 to -1.06962. The old vanna is the right one divided by the discount.

The theta and vanna references in `testBachelierCalculatorGreeks` matched the previous formulas (spot 98 vs forward 100, discount 0.95), so I updated them. The new test checks both against finite differences with non-zero carry, for a call and a put; it fails before the change and passes after.
